historical_context.time_period: Kalsa's standing present; the present date, calendar, and interval since the road office withdrew remain unresolved.
historical_context.location: The existing final depot below the last imperial cut toward the fogbound Luck Crown, with a lower hosted approach, roofed court, upper stair, and seeping retaining wall.
historical_context.summary: A local depot witness opens a sealed volume for a Ju'onai recovery audit and discovers the guide-pay book, later reused for road orders, where the claimant expected the final office ledger. An approaching porter train and unstable upper cut force record custody, passage, labor claims, and shelter costs to bite before title can be decided.

public_facts.text: The Ju'onai road office reached the Selza'a plateau more than once but did not keep a permanent self-supporting office; the works left numbered stones, cut paths, damaged catchments, abandoned depots, and unpaid guide claims.
The final depot contains unpaid guide claims, and one numbered stone above it has been turned toward the plateau.
Selza'a country has no central government; territorial families answer for paths, stores, hosted entry, and shared work through local arrangements.
Road travel in Kalsa depends on water, shelter, warning marks, negotiated passage, dangerous weather, and authorities that do not collapse into road ownership.

ambient_pressures.text: The recovered volume can support unpaid labor, depot-store, and later road-order claims without becoming a deed over the road or a complete closing inventory.
Ju'onai administrative competence depends on persistent records and bounded portfolios, but class power enters through who frames the system and controls the archive used for appeal.
Selza'a host families can withhold passage and maintain warnings, while unpaid workers, guests, and present dependents retain claims that a territorial closure cannot erase.
The road crisis has no valid magical shortcut: coincidence, survival, or well-timed recovery cannot identify Luck or authorize blame.

groups.label: Final depot hosts, guide claimants, and current users
institutional_logic: Keep hosted crossings, warning, shelter, old labor claims, and present territorial limits legible without creating a central road owner.
material_incentives: Protect the upper cut and catchment
internal_shames: Hiding a book that workers need
Opening a dangerous cut for prestige
Calling guests protected while leaving them in fog
prestige_markers: A warning that reaches the lower path
A hosted crossing that creates no permanent command
taboo_triggers: An imperial seal treated as passage
A guide claim translated into collaboration
A host using protection to erase a guest's claim
emotional_display_norms: Fear appears as dry work humor, hands on cords and records, rapid shelter preparation, and refusal to certify more than a witness saw.
trust_defaults: Trusts maintained route marks, current material inspection, duplicate records, and witnesses more than inherited office language or claims of lucky timing.

groups.label: Ju'onai road recovery audit and claimant pressure
institutional_logic: Recover the office record chain, separate valid intervention from local obstruction, and test whether the road portfolio ever lawfully ended.
material_incentives: Avoid inheriting a wall failure as office liability
internal_shames: An audit captured by its sponsor
An elegant office claim defeated by wet stone
prestige_markers: A recovered portfolio that can answer its debts
taboo_triggers: Local witnesses denying the seal any force
A host compact making imperial measurement irrelevant
Evidence that the office improved a road and abandoned its workers
emotional_display_norms: Alarm is compressed into warrants, seals, system boundaries, and increasingly narrow accusations of obstruction.
trust_defaults: Trusts authenticated chains and comparative records, but risks mistaking archival continuity for territorial authority.

groups.label: Porters and current road users called onto the ascent
institutional_logic: Reach shelter and deliver loads under a route sequence someone else represented as current.
material_incentives: Receive warning before the upper cut
Avoid carrying handcarts onto a failing wall
Have delay charged to the caller rather than the carriers
internal_virtues: Visible receipts for delay and loss
internal_shames: Being used as a fait accompli for a road claim
prestige_markers: A train brought under roof intact
A hold cost assigned to the office that created it
taboo_triggers: An upper seal overruling a warning heard on the lower path
Being called unauthorized after following the claimant's own sequence
emotional_display_norms: Urgency arrives through chimes, cart noise, wet loads, clipped route reports, and impatience with ownership arguments conducted under a dry roof.
trust_defaults: Trusts current warning relays, visible road condition, and whoever provides shelter; may distrust both host and auditor for the dangerous summons.

cultural_pressure_fields.summary: The depot must keep the upper cut closed when material danger requires it without letting closure erase unpaid work, guest needs, or the audit trail.
cultural_pressure_fields.projection_use: Give Ari choices among copying, inspection, warning, shelter, refusal, and transfer; each protects one owner while exposing another claim or cost.

cultural_pressure_fields.summary: The audit needs a coherent record chain, but every step that makes the book easier to carry upward can detach it from workers, current hazards, and the local authorities the old road never abolished.
cultural_pressure_fields.projection_use: Make Oren value receipts and original custody while remaining capable of recognizing a documented material stop; do not make him a caricature or a universal judge.

cultural_pressure_fields.summary: The approaching train turns abstract title into immediate shelter, load, wall, and delay costs borne by people who did not choose the audit.
cultural_pressure_fields.projection_use: Let chimes and handcart arrival change options and visible state before any archive claim is resolved.

observer_read: Local custody protecting a useful record
Possible obstruction disguised as territorial care
target_self_read: People preserving wages, shelter, and present road safety after the office withdrew
misread_patterns: Treats refusal to transfer as refusal to inspect
Treats a current host warning as a rival road office
Underweights claims that lack imperial form
factional_misread_matrix.projection_use: Let Oren's best administrative language remain useful and coercive at once; Ari can correct scope but cannot make the audit harmless.

observer_read: The old road returning through a book
An office searching for title in unpaid labor
target_self_read: A bounded recovery process capable of preserving claims beyond one mountain court
misread_patterns: May treat every receipt as seizure
May ignore that superior review can preserve a claim local power would bury
May confuse Oren's warrant with the claimant's full intent
factional_misread_matrix.projection_use: Keep local suspicion sharp but not omniscient; Oren's chain can protect evidence even while empowering the claimant.

role_pressure_fields.summary: A local witness for one crossing watch who controls present entries, copies, warning maintenance, and initial book custody without owning the claims inside them.
obligations: Avoid making shelter depend on agreement
failure_modes: Protecting the book at the expense of people
Issuing a warning no lower relay receives

role_pressure_fields.summary: A claimant carrying family testimony and witness cords for labor the former road office used and did not pay.
obligations: Preserve a copy outside imperial custody
failure_modes: Protecting family standing while poorer workers vanish from the copy

role_pressure_fields.summary: A Ju'onai auditor empowered to recover and receipt records, not to decide passage or make a sponsor's portfolio claim true.
failure_modes: Letting the sponsor choose the frame
Reading reused leaves as uninterrupted authority
Taking the original before claims have separate witnesses

role_pressure_fields.summary: The worker who controls the court's current stores, roof space, load rails, and hospitality costs while other offices contest the road.
obligations: Record who created the emergency cost
failure_modes: Letting the archive dispute consume stores without account

known_context.text: Ari knows the local custody terms, current records, warning system, host marks, and only the material wall condition Ari personally inspects or hears.

beliefs.text: Ari believes a useful record keeps owners separable and a warning must reach bodies before an appeal can vindicate it.

misreads.text: Ari may treat Oren's demand for a clean chain as claimant loyalty even when he is trying to preserve several claims in a portable form.

must_not_know.text: Ari must not know whether Luck caused the recovery or what superior Ju'onai review will decide.

known_context.text: Tera knows her inherited witness cords, guide-pay claims, local road memory, and what the old office failed to pay; she does not own every claimant's story.

beliefs.text: Tera believes removing the original before copies are witnessed lets office continuity swallow labor evidence.

misreads.text: Tera may read any audit custody as erasure and underweight the danger of one local family controlling the only book.

must_not_know.text: Tera must not know the auditor's private sponsor instructions or treat inherited recitation as complete author history.

known_context.text: Oren knows his warrant, old and current seals, administrative record practice, the leaves he reads, and material evidence admitted into his receipt.

beliefs.text: Oren believes an original under traceable custody can preserve claims beyond a local dispute, while an unbounded refusal may let the strongest host keep the archive.

misreads.text: Oren may treat a maintained territorial warning as obstruction because the old road sequence gives it no legible office owner.

must_not_know.text: Oren must not infer safe passage, legal portfolio continuity, intent, or Luck from the recovered seal alone.

known_context.text: Mara knows the depot's actual roof, stores, load lanes, lower arch, and immediate shelter capacity.

beliefs.text: Mara believes the people called into danger need shelter before claimants finish assigning its cost.

misreads.text: Mara may dismiss slow record work until a missing copy turns current generosity into unowned debt.

must_not_know.text: Mara must not know the train's exact condition before a chime or arrival makes it observable.

author_only_boundaries.text: Luck's backstage operation remains unavailable to the characters. The audit, wall seepage, warning, and book recovery have no adopted magical cause.
The fixture-authored depot court, witness role, closure cord, present characters, and mixed ledger are one local elaboration, not a universal Selza'a road institution.
The old road's final ownership, exact geography, historical actors, campaign count, and any surviving Ju'onai portfolio remain unresolved outside this present audit pressure.

open_questions.question: Which office or compact will ultimately hear the wage, road-portfolio, and territorial-passage claims?
open_questions.notes: The fixture ends with evidence and present hazard redistributed, not with a universal court invented to settle the dispute.

open_questions.question: Does the upper retaining wall fail after the watch, and what repair compact owns the catchment above it?
open_questions.notes: The scene uses visible seepage, moved chalk beads, grit, and audible stone movement while leaving final structural outcome and wider work ownership open.

open_questions.question: Does any present Ju'onai authority recognize the claimant's old road portfolio?
open_questions.notes: Oren can recover the record chain and argue scope; he cannot settle present recognition inside the depot.
